tasks.title: First squares
tasks.statement: Write a function first_squares(n): a list of the first n squares of natural numbers: 1, 4, 9, … Use itertools.count and islice.
tasks.hint: list(islice((x * x for x in count(1)), n)).

tasks.title: Chain the lists
tasks.statement: Write a function chain_all(*lists): one list with the elements of all the given lists in order. Use itertools.chain.
tasks.hint: list(chain(*lists)): the star unpacks the arguments further.

tasks.title: Records so far
tasks.statement: Write a function running_max(nums): a list of the running maximum: for 3, 1, 4, 1, 5 it is 3, 3, 4, 4, 5. Use accumulate with the function max.

tasks.title: Group sizes
tasks.statement: Write a function group_sizes(words): a dictionary mapping the first letter to how many words start with it. Use groupby, and remember that the data must be sorted.
tasks.hint: for k, g in groupby(sorted(words), key=lambda w: w[0]): result[k] = len(list(g)).

tasks.title: All pairs
tasks.statement: Write a function all_pairs(items): a list of all pairs of distinct elements (each pair once, in the order of the list) as tuples. Use itertools.combinations.

tasks.title: All passwords
tasks.statement: Write a function passwords(alphabet, length): a list of all strings of the given length made of the characters of alphabet (with repeats), in lexicographic order of the alphabet. Use itertools.product.

tasks.title: Compressing repeats
tasks.statement: Write a function rle(s): compression of consecutive repeats in a string, as a list of tuples (character, how many times in a row): for "aaabcc" it is [('a', 3), ('b', 1), ('c', 2)]. Use groupby without sorting.
tasks.hint: [(k, len(list(g))) for k, g in groupby(s)].

tasks.title: Differences of neighbors
tasks.statement: Write a function diffs(nums): a list of differences between neighboring elements: for 1, 4, 9, 16 it is 3, 5, 7. Use itertools.pairwise.
tasks.hint: [b - a for a, b in pairwise(nums)].

tasks.title: While the numbers are small
tasks.statement: Write a function small_prefix(nums, limit): the initial piece of the list while the elements are less than limit; stop at the first element that is greater than or equal to it. Use itertools.takewhile.
